chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'Indeed, Allah has made the good heavy upon the people of the world, like its heaviness in their scales on the Day of Resurrection; and indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made the evil light upon the people of the world, like its lightness in their scales on the Day of Resurrection.'
ai.seo_question: How does Allah make good and evil deeds feel in this world compared to the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the divine wisdom behind the perception of deeds in this world, noting that Allah makes good deeds feel 'heavy' with significance and evil deeds feel 'light' with ease, directly mirroring their actual weight in the scales of the Day of Judgment. This hadith, found in al-Kafi, highlights the concept of *thiqal* (heaviness) and *khiffah* (lightness) as spiritual realities that encourage believers to cherish righteous actions while making sin appear trivial and easy to commit, thus serving as both an incentive for virtue and a subtle warning against negligence.
